exposure: Mode of delivery (elective caesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
Presence of bacteria in placental tissue
Presence of bacteria in amniotic fluid, vernix caseosa, saliva, vaginal, and rectal samples
outcome: Presence and origin of placental microbiome
cohort: 76 women with full-term pregnancies (50 elective caesarean deliveries and 26 vaginal deliveries)
finding: The study found no evidence to support the existence of a distinct placental microbiome in healthy term pregnancies, suggesting that previously reported bacterial presence in the placenta might be due to contamination or low-grade bacterial presence.
mod_finding: Bacterial cultures showed more bacteria in placentas from vaginal deliveries compared to cesarean deliveries, suggesting potential contamination from the vaginal environment during labor.
